\par
\noindent $\Delta_{\rm self}=u_A(1)-u_B^{\rm self}$ compares separate conditions; $\Delta_{\rm table}=u_A(1)-u_B(5)$ compares seats in the same mixed games.
Mixed entries average ten games; resident self-play averages twenty. $\rho_N$ is fixation probability from one entrant in a population of size $N$, using all table compositions and $\beta=1$, not just the first payoff gap. Neutral fixation is $1/N$. These comparisons do not establish evolutionary stability.\par

\noindent Outcomes weight each retained model's self-play by its stationary mass; uniform assigns equal weight to retained models. These are rare-mutation monomorphic outcomes, not success rates during invasion. At $p=0.5$, zero contribution and an exact target both attain welfare 20, although their target rates are 0 and 100\%. Low target rate alone therefore does not imply welfare loss.\par
